clue.text: Nymph carrying an orchid

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth a water nymph pursued by the river god Alpheus became a spring in Sicily
a genus of North American bog orchid, the dragon's-mouth or swamp pink, bears this nymph's name

explanation.surface: A woodland sprite with a flower tucked under her arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The same classical name belongs both to the Nereid of legend and to a small genus of pink bog orchids.

clue.text: Disparage, though not very well

definitions.meaning: to belittle or criticise someone, as a two-word phrasal verb
... describes someone tired, below par and slightly ill

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a person who is feeling under the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means to belittle; as an adjective it means exhausted and in poor health.

clue.text: If he appears again, may get a beating

definitions.text: If he appears again, may get a beating

parts.words: If he appears again, may get a beating
parts.note: a male cat's name written twice over gives a small drum that is struck with the hands

explanation.surface: A threat: let this fellow show his face again and he will be thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ruffian warned off; doubling the name gives tom-tom, a drum, which is what gets beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating this name makes the word for a hand-beaten drum, so the doubled fellow is struck.

clue.text: Green suit is patched — no replacement required

indicators.note: a replacement puts things in new places, so the letters of 'suit is patched' and 'no' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tatty green suit has been mended, so there is no need to buy a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patched' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder: 'replacement required' rearranges SUIT IS PATCHED with NO, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the sense of naive or inexperienced, lacking worldly polish.

clue.text: Star letter written in Greek

definitions.meaning: the brightest star in a constellation is designated by the first Greek letter, as in the Centauri system
the opening character of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A celebrity's fan mail composed in Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers label a constellation's leading star with this first character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Soil upturned is contaminated

indicators.note: read as 'up' plus 'turned': up is added to the soil word and the whole run is turned backwards

parts.note: soil means dirt, and the word 'up' from upturned sits after it

explanation.surface: Earth that has been dug over turns out to be polluted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' splits as UP + 'turned': DIRT UP read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rotten and foul-smelling is spoilt or tainted, close to contaminated in sense.

clue.text: Dislocate toe in Pinter play — "the ambassador"

indicators.note: to dislocate is to put out of place, so the letters of the following words are moved around

explanation.surface: Stage direction for an actor in a Harold Pinter drama, playing the ambassador, to put out a toe.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Pinter was a British playwright; all fifteen letters of TOE IN PINTER PLAY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat given full powers to act on behalf of a government, such as an envoy or ambassador.

clue.text: Stopping scramble into minaret

indicators.note: a scramble mixes things up, so the letters of 'into minaret' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stops a frantic climb up into a mosque tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopping as a noun means bringing to an end, a cessation or conclusion.

clue.text: Position taken by everyone on fashionable street

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places the word for everyone after the fashionable street

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everybody has gathered on a trendy street to claim a spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To position equipment or a person is to set them in place, to put in.

clue.text: Hostility's a problem in a recession

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the words for problem, in and a are read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: An economic downturn is causing bad feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' turns SUM IN A backwards. The first 'a' and the 's of 'Hostility's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling of enmity or ill will towards someone, the Latin for spirit used in English for animosity.

clue.text: On round table, this pastry has decorative effect

definitions.text: On round table, this pastry has decorative effect

parts.words: On round table, this pastry has decorative effect
parts.note: a style of round antique table has a scalloped raised rim that resembles the crimped edge of a pie

explanation.surface: A tart set on a circular table makes it look pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: A furniture term: a round tilt-top table with a crimped raised rim is named after the pastry it resembles.
explanation.definitionFit: The baked pastry shell of a pie lends its name to a decorative scalloped table edge.

clue.text: Food transport vehicles

parts.note: the tubes in the body that carry swallowed food from the throat to the stomach

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests delivery lorries; the vehicles are anatomical, the gullets that convey food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gullets are the muscular passages through which swallowed food travels down to the stomach.

clue.text: One who is unconsciously pedestrian?

parts.note: a person who walks about while not awake, taken literally as an unconscious pedestrian

explanation.walkthrough: 'pedestrian' suggests dull, but here it means someone on foot, doing so in their sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A somnambulist walks while asleep, literally a pedestrian without consciousness.

clue.text: I fled the country

parts.note: fled means ran away

explanation.surface: Someone escaped from the land of their birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation, formerly Persia, is an instance of a country.

clue.text: Keen to hand around the joint

indicators.note: to hand around is to pass things out in different directions, so the letters of 'Keen' are redistributed

explanation.surface: Someone eager to pass the cannabis cigarette round the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette passed round; it is a body joint. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge between thigh and shin is a body joint.

clue.text: Inescapable — a born exile must travel around!

indicators.note: travelling around moves things from place to place, so the letters of 'a born exile' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A banished person's fate is to wander, with no way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Relentless and impossible to avoid or stop, as an unstoppable fate.

clue.text: Retire in the main

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea, and the sea retires when its tide goes out

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly'; it means 'at sea', where the tide withdraws.
explanation.definitionFit: The outgoing tide is the sea retreating, so the sea's retiring is this tidal movement.

clue.text: Playing piano, claim to be in harmony

indicators.note: playing about with something moves it around, so P and 'claim to be' are mixed up

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A musician at the keyboard insists the ensemble is in tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges P (piano) with CLAIM TO BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to coexist or work together without conflict, agreeing well.

clue.text: Result of discovering an escape route?

definitions.text: Result of discovering an escape route?

parts.words: Result of discovering an escape route?
parts.note: read as two words, finding a way out lets you come out, while the whole means a consequence

explanation.walkthrough: Split it into OUT + COME, which is what you can do once you have found an escape route; as one word it means a result.
explanation.definitionFit: A consequence or end product of events, the way something turns out.

clue.text: Move slowly, attending church

parts.note: attending means present, in, as in 'in class'

explanation.surface: Congregation shuffling forward during a service.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep forward a little at a time, by small increments.

clue.text: French artist and film director portraying commandant in acute distress?

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer, a commandant

indicators.note: distress suggests something disturbed, so the letters of 'acute' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A film-maker depicts a military commander in great anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acute distress' reads as one phrase about anguish, but 'distress' alone scrambles the word before it into CTEAU, and 'in' sets the officer there; 'portraying' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Cocteau was a French poet, artist and film-maker, director of La Belle et la Bete.

clue.text: Mount from Vietnam lacking vigour

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letters for vigour are removed from Vietnam

parts.note: vim means vigour or energy

explanation.surface: A tired mountain in Southeast Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes V, I and M, scattered but in order, from VIETNAM. 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is a mountain, and Mount is a crossword staple for a peak.

clue.text: In a rigid stupor? Tom needs a stimulant!

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a tonic is a stimulant or pick-me-up

explanation.surface: Tom is so dazed and stiff that he needs a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name; it is a tomcat. 'needs' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the state of immobile, unresponsive rigidity seen in catatonia.

clue.text: Giant fish

definitions.meaning: a large ugly creature of Scandinavian folklore
to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat

explanation.surface: A huge fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norse monster of great size, and as a verb a way of fishing by drawing a lure through water.

clue.text: Illegal Aussie look-out man getting bird

definitions.meaning: Australian slang for a person keeping watch during an illegal activity such as a two-up game

explanation.surface: A lawbreaking Australian lookout acquires a parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: Australian slang names a lookout for gamblers after the crested parrot, said to post sentries while the flock feeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A crested parrot of Australia, and in Australian slang a sentry for illicit gambling.

clue.text: Sportsman ran with leg injury

indicators.note: an injury distorts or damages, so the letters of 'ran' and 'leg' are rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete kept running despite hurting his leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injury' rearranges RAN and LEG together; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman who uses rod and line, someone pursuing a field sport.

clue.text: Petition directed heavenwards to Egyptian god

indicators.note: in a down clue going upwards towards heaven means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to petition is to beg

explanation.surface: A prayer sent up to a deity of ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Egyptian religion he was the earth god, father of Osiris.

clue.text: Red sea in trouble — dried up

indicators.note: something in trouble is disturbed, so the letters of 'Red sea' are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The Red Sea is in difficulty because it has dried out.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorched or parched by intense heat, burnt dry.

clue.text: Loafer? Was resting before a wrestling match!

parts.note: lay is the past tense of lie, so it means was resting
a bout is a single contest in wrestling or boxing

explanation.surface: An idler had a lie-down before a wrestling bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loafer' might be a shoe; the question mark points to a lazy person. 'before' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle, work-shy person who loafs about doing nothing.
